items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee personally led a massive ~4-km anti-SIR march through Kolkata on Tuesday afternoon — the march her TMC faction had announced for Rajabazar to Park Circus at ~2 PM — walking with a copy of the Indian Constitution, accompanied by TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and city religious/community leaders and celebrities. She accused the BJP and the Election Commission of colluding to disenfranchise two crore Bengal voters via SIR as 'silent, invisible rigging', mockingly called CEC Gyanesh Kumar 'kursi babu', and warned the Modi government's fall would be 'inevitable' if even one eligible voter is deleted. Counter-side: BJP's Suvendu Adhikari led a rival 'Parivartan Yatra' (Sodepur to Agarpara, 2 km), daring the TMC to stop the exercise and demanding every infiltrator be deported. Context: the SIR rollout formally began in Bengal the same day — 80,000+ booth-level officers, 16 lakh+ enumeration forms distributed on day one.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee personally leads massive anti-SIR rally through Kolkata as Bengal's SIR rollout begins

items.summary: The same report says at least two deaths by suicide were reported in Bengal on Tuesday and linked by families to SIR panic: Jahir Mal of Khalisani, Uluberia (found hanging; family says he was under severe stress over a spelling error in an official document) and farmer Mohan Sheikh of Kandi (pesticide; family says his name was missing from the 2002 rolls and he feared deportation). Mamata Banerjee claimed seven people have died in connection with the exercise so far; Adhikari countered that the TMC is falsely linking deaths to derail the EC's process and said the CM should be held responsible for deaths from 'misplaced panic'. Single-sourced and uncorroborated — treat as unverified.
items.title: Reports allege SIR-panic suicides in Bengal on Tuesday (unverified)
